cat > deck.md <<'EOF'
# Small 3-Year Revenue Model

## Slide 1 — Executive summary
- A simple, volume-driven model forecasts revenue growing from **$120k in Year 1** to **$360k in Year 3**.
- Growth comes from more customers, higher average revenue per customer (ARPC), and modest expansion revenue.

## Slide 2 — Model structure
- Core formula: **Revenue = Ending customers × ARPC**.
- Customer roll-forward: **Ending customers = Beginning customers + New customers − Churned customers**.
- Churn is modeled as a percentage of beginning customers; ARPC grows annually with pricing and mix.

## Slide 3 — Key assumptions
| Assumption | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Beginning customers | 100 | 140 | 200 |
| New customers | 50 | 80 | 120 |
| Annual churn | 10% | 10% | 10% |
| Ending customers | 140 | 200 | 288 |
| ARPC | $857 | $1,200 | $1,250 |

## Slide 4 — Revenue build
| Metric | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Ending customers | 140 | 200 | 288 |
| ARPC | $857 | $1,200 | $1,250 |
| Revenue | **$120k** | **$240k** | **$360k** |
| Year-over-year growth | — | 100% | 50% |

## Slide 5 — Interpretation
- Revenue doubles in Year 2 as customer additions accelerate and ARPC steps up.
- Year 3 growth moderates to 50% but remains strong because the installed customer base compounds.
- The model is intentionally small: changing new customers, churn, or ARPC immediately updates the revenue outlook.

## Slide 6 — Sensitivities and watch-outs
- **Upside:**
